entries.title: How do I check my terminal arrival window and the port-of-call day?
entries.text: Kriativos On Board takes place November 20–23, 2026, on MSC Musica, departing from and returning to Santos, with a port of call in Búzios. Check the day and time of the port of call, your terminal arrival window and the boarding instructions in your booking's itinerary and voucher. Don't use the charter bus schedule as the ship's schedule.

entries.title: Who requests the cabin vouchers, when and through which channel?
entries.text: Royal Trip handles issuing the group check-in. When Júnior announces it in the official group, the person responsible for the cabin should message him privately to receive the vouchers and luggage tags as PDFs. Check the details of all passengers and print the documents. Follow the agency's announcements; there's no confirmed release date.

entries.title: Which document should I bring? Is an old RG or a digital CNH accepted?
entries.text: For Brazilians on this domestic itinerary, MSC accepts the RG (Brazilian ID card), the CNH (Brazilian driver's license), a passport and other civil documents allowed under its official rules, as long as the ID is valid and has a recognizable photo. For this itinerary, MSC doesn't require an RG issued less than ten years ago. A digital CNH must be opened in the official app; screenshots, photos and copies don't replace the document. Preferably, also bring the physical document and keep your voucher and ID at hand.
entries.keywords: Documents for boarding

entries.title: What documents do I need for minors or foreign passengers?
entries.text: Confirm with Royal Trip the documents and authorizations that apply based on the passenger's age, the guardians traveling with the minor, nationality and residence. Ask for the correct form when an authorization is required, and have everything ready before the trip. Don't send personal documents through the public questions form.

entries.title: I'm pregnant: what arrangements and medical certificate should I send to the agency?
entries.text: MSC doesn't allow travel if the pregnancy reaches 24 weeks at any point during the cruise. Below that limit, it requires a medical certificate stating fitness to travel and a low-risk pregnancy, with the gestational age, the estimated due date, the doctor's CRM (Brazilian medical license number), signature and stamp. Let Royal Trip know in advance so they can forward the documents and review your booking.

entries.title: How do I check that my baby is included in the cabin and request a crib?
entries.text: All passengers, including babies, must be listed on the cabin booking. The mini-cruise allows babies to take part according to MSC rules for this cruise length. Confirm fares, fees, crib availability and other conditions with Royal Trip; don't assume it's free or that a fare applies automatically by age.

entries.title: Do I need to show a Covid-19 vaccination or test?
entries.text: Check with Royal Trip and MSC the health requirements in effect for your sailing. Don't treat the old two-dose or antigen-test rules as current instructions. Requirements may change depending on the health situation, the destination and decisions by the authorities; follow the official guidance you receive for your boarding.

entries.title: What is MSC's luggage allowance?
entries.text: Per person: two bags of up to 23 kg each, measuring up to 90 × 75 × 43 cm, and two carry-on pieces of up to 10 kg each, measuring up to 56 × 45 × 25 cm. Per cabin, the total can't exceed 100 kg and/or eight pieces. Also check your ticket and the specific limits for flights and ground transportation.
entries.keywords: Luggage allowance

entries.title: How do I check my bags and what stays with me?
entries.text: Attach the tags you received from the agency to your checked bags and follow the staff's directions at the terminal. Keep documents, valuables, medications and essentials in your carry-on: your bags may reach the cabin later.

entries.title: What's prohibited? Can I bring a hair dryer, flat iron or drone?
entries.text: MSC prohibits bringing on board any beverages, alcoholic or not (the exception is factory-sealed water for medical devices or infant formula), weapons, sharp objects such as blades and scissors, illegal drugs (including medical marijuana), flammable materials and explosives, and items that heat up or have an open flame, such as clothes irons, kettles, candles and incense. Hair dryers and flat irons are allowed. Drones may be carried if stored in your cabin, but using them on board is prohibited; ashore, local rules apply. Inflatables, such as air mattresses and rafts, can't be inflated on board. Alcohol bought in onboard shops or ashore is held by security until the end of the cruise. For food, MSC makes an exception for packaged, industrially processed dry foods. Prohibited items found at screening are confiscated and not returned; check the full official list and the conditions for special needs.

entries.title: What does the cabin provide and what should I bring?
entries.text: The cabin provides bed linens, towels, liquid soap, shampoo, a hair dryer, TV, air conditioning and a safe. Bring your personal toiletries, including a toothbrush, toothpaste and conditioner, plus sunscreen and a compatible plug adapter if needed. Check the equipment and amenities of your booked category with the agency. The minibar doesn't guarantee suitable refrigeration for medications.

entries.title: How does the official KOB charter bus work?
entries.text: The charter bus runs round trip between Barra Funda, in São Paulo, and the Port of Santos. The meeting point is on Rua Tagipuru, near No. 552, behind the Memorial da América Latina. Bus 1: meet at 6:00 AM, departure at 6:30 AM, grace period until 6:40 AM. Bus 2: meet at 6:40 AM, departure at 7:20 AM, grace period until 7:30 AM. Arrive at the meeting time; the grace period isn't a new departure time. Check which bus is assigned to your booking. Bus 1 is confirmed. Bus 2 and any other buses depend on a minimum number of passengers; if it isn't reached, the operation provides for a full refund via Pix (Brazil's instant payment system). The return from the Port of Santos on Nov 23 is scheduled for 10:30 AM. Check the current terms on the official charter bus page.

entries.title: I'm flying in. Is there a KOB bus at Congonhas or Guarulhos?
entries.text: The KOB charter bus leaves from Barra Funda, not from the airports. If you'll rely on road transportation to Santos, Guarulhos may be an option; Congonhas and Viracopos are also alternatives. Before buying or planning your route, check with the airline and Viação Cometa about routes, final destination, schedules and availability for the date. If you arrive at the Santos bus terminal (Rodoviária de Santos), plan an extra transfer to Concais. Allow extra time for traffic, lines and the holiday; the times mentioned are estimates.

entries.title: I'm driving. What should I do about parking?
entries.text: The official Concais parking can be reserved in advance. Check availability, rates, the access address and instructions directly with the terminal before you leave (concais.com.br). When you arrive, follow the staff's directions for checking your bags.

entries.title: Can I use my cabin as soon as I board?
entries.text: Cabins may still be getting ready. They may be released around 1:00 or 2:00 PM; wait for MSC's announcement. While you wait, check out the buffet options and keep what you need with you until your bags arrive. Go by the announcement the ship actually makes.

entries.title: Is the safety drill mandatory?
entries.text: Yes. Complete the mandatory procedure MSC indicates for your boarding. The crew will share the location, time and steps, including instructions in the app. Don't assume that watching a video or opening the app, on its own, covers all your obligations.

entries.title: Where and when do I pick up my kit? What's in it?
entries.text: The meet-up and kit pickup are planned for 4:00/4:30 PM on the first day at the Crystal Lounge; the room and time will be confirmed in the official group. The kit includes a badge/lanyard, a wristband, a collectible commemorative coin and a sturdy tote bag from Fácil Shopping. Check the announcements before heading to the meet-up.

entries.title: Where do I find the event schedule and announcements?
entries.text: Look for the bulletin board at the entrance to the game room and follow the event's official group. MSC's daily program lists the ship's services and activities. Check these channels for changes and confirmations; this guide covers preparation and doesn't replace onboard announcements.

entries.title: How do I confirm the room, the table hours and the Sunday return deadline?
entries.text: The Crystal Lounge is the space planned for KOB. The room still depends on MSC's confirmation. Extended gaming hours are expected during the day and at night, according to the event schedule. Tables are open to everyone, on a rotating basis. On Sunday, we'll announce the deadline for returning the game library titles and clearing the tables for the final inventory.

entries.title: How do I register my attendance on Guru and find games and game teachers?
entries.text: Board Game Guru is the event's app for games and giveaways, available for Android and iOS. Open the Kriativos On Board page and tap ‘I’m going’. You can also browse titles, filters, game teachers who explain rules and games shared by attendees. The app's official website is boardgameguru.app.

entries.title: I can't use the app. Can I take part in the giveaways?
entries.text: Look for the Encounter team to request manual inclusion on the list and confirm your registration. To enter the giveaways, tap ‘I’m going’ or register your attendance with the game teachers. Follow the official group for the rules and times as they're announced.

entries.title: Can I bring games and prototypes, favorite titles and share my collection?
entries.text: Yes. Register the games you plan to bring in the app, including by importing them from Ludopedia or BoardGameGeek, and favorite the titles you want to play to help the game teachers plan. Label your games and stay within your baggage allowance. Those who share the most games may receive prizes and surprises; we'll announce the criteria in the official group. Prototypes can be shared, but a formal activity depends on the event schedule.

entries.title: How do I check out games, and can I use them outside the room?
entries.text: Follow the game teachers' instructions for checkout, care and return. When you take a game from the game library outside the room, register your name and cabin with the team for tracking; the title is your responsibility. Use permitted areas and don't take up restaurant tables with games. Return everything by the deadline announced for the inventory.

entries.title: I've booked and want to join a table: how do I find game teachers and activities?
entries.text: Look for the Encounter game teachers to pick games, learn rules and find people to play with. On Guru, you can also see who knows each title. Check the bulletin board for activities and tournaments as they're confirmed. You don't need to arrive with a group already formed.

entries.title: What should I wear? Do I need formal attire?
entries.text: Bring comfortable clothes and shoes for the day and for gaming, plus a light jacket for the wind and the air conditioning. For dinner, wear neat casual or smart casual; the main restaurant doesn't allow tank tops or flip-flops. Check the ship's guidance for each venue and night. You don't need a suit or a formal gown.

entries.title: How do I prepare for the themes and check party times and locations?
entries.text: The White Party is on the schedule; bring something white if you'd like to join. For the KOB closing on Sunday night, the theme is the 80s, with retro pieces, neon and accessories. Themed outfits are optional. Confirm times and locations in the schedule; a private space for a costume party depends on the ship's authorization.

entries.title: Where can I check meal times and alternatives to my dinner seating?
entries.text: Your booking includes full board as purchased, with meals at the buffet and the main restaurant. There are pizza options at extended hours, close to 24 hours a day, but the confirmed hours for each service appear in the MSC daily program. Don't assume the entire buffet runs nonstop. Specialty restaurants and extras are charged separately.

entries.title: How does my dinner seating work? What if I'm late?
entries.text: Check your Cruise Card for the seating and table assigned for the main restaurant. Arrive on time: the 15-minute grace period refers to kitchen orders. If you miss your seating, check the buffet and pizzeria alternatives in the daily program. The times mentioned are examples and don't replace the seating on your booking.

entries.title: Can I have dinner with friends from other cabins?
entries.text: Right after boarding, find the restaurant's maître d' with the numbers of the cabins that want to sit together and ask for the tables to be combined. The team will confirm whether there's still room at dinner.

entries.title: I've already chosen a package: how do I check the cabin rules and the daily limit?
entries.text: It's optional. The options mentioned are Non-Alcoholic, Easy and Premium Extra; confirm the packages available for your sailing. If one adult purchases a package, the other adults in the cabin must follow the same package rule; children and teens follow the non-alcoholic option for their age, with exceptions for babies according to MSC. Easy and Premium Extra include up to 15 alcoholic drinks per person from 6:00 AM to 6:00 AM the next day. Confirm price, deadline, discounts and installment options with Royal Trip.
entries.keywords: Drink packages

entries.title: Is the minibar included in Premium Extra?
entries.text: No. Having a minibar in your cabin doesn't mean its products are part of the drink package: items consumed from the minibar are charged separately. You can store drinks picked up at the bars as allowed by your package; check whether the service will be available and how it works.

entries.title: How do I buy internet access? Can I transfer or share it? Will my phone work in Búzios?
entries.text: Internet access beyond the ship's network is purchased separately. MSC packages are personal and tied to the activated devices; choose how many devices you plan to use, since replacing a device that's already registered isn't allowed. Don't count on transferring or sharing an individual package. In Búzios, there may be signal from Brazilian carriers, depending on coverage and location. Check the port-of-call day in your booking and your carrier's terms.

entries.title: Can I use MSC for Me and the chat without an internet package?
entries.text: Connect to the ship's internal Wi-Fi to use the available MSC for Me features. The onboard chat doesn't require an external internet package; MSC lists the service for guests over 16. Add ‘Kriativo’ to your name or nickname so your friends can find you more easily. Check which features are available on MSC Musica and follow the onboard instructions.

entries.title: How do I pay for onboard expenses? Are Wise/Nomad and installments accepted?
entries.text: Onboard purchases are recorded on the account linked to your Cruise Card. Confirm with MSC/reception which methods are accepted to link or pay this account, the currency and any deposits. If you plan to use an international card, check that it's enabled and accepted, and bring the physical card. Wise, Nomad and installments may be available, but confirm availability, criteria and conditions before counting on them. The cabin price in Brazilian reais and the currency for onboard spending are separate matters.

entries.title: How do I check which specialty restaurants are operating and book them on this sailing?
entries.text: They're extra services, separate from full board. Kaito Sushi Bar and Butcher’s Cut are options that have been mentioned; MSC lists Butcher’s Cut on MSC Musica with a planned start in November 2026. Confirm which restaurants will be operating on your sailing, how to book and the onboard prices.

entries.title: What should I check in the insurance offer and policy?
entries.text: Insurance is optional and recommended for unforeseen events and private medical expenses. The approximate price is R$ 112.00 per person, with a cancellation condition covering 29 reasons, and it must be purchased up to twenty days before boarding. Ask Royal Trip for the current policy and offer, and confirm price, deadline, coverage, exclusions, currency and assistance before purchasing.

entries.title: My medication needs refrigeration, or I need an accommodation. What should I do?
entries.text: Let Royal Trip know in advance, through a private channel, so they can forward your need to MSC and confirm the arrangements. Don't assume the cabin minibar keeps the temperature your medication requires. Pack your medications and personal instructions in your carry-on. Don't send prescriptions, medical reports or diagnoses through the general questions form.

entries.title: How does the kids club work? Does the staff change diapers or provide meals?
entries.text: MSC offers kids' activities by age group; hours and sign-up should be checked on board. The Doremi Club runs from about 9:00 AM to 11:00 PM. Children in diapers must be accompanied, since kids club activities don't include diaper changes or meals. Confirm these conditions with the MSC Musica youth staff: services like Baby Care have their own rules and shouldn't be confused with the kids club. Plan the child's care and meals with their parent or guardian.

entries.title: Are water, tea and coffee free? Will we have the Aqua system?
entries.text: The buffet offers water, tea and coffee dispensers, subject to the service's operating hours. The Aqua system may offer refillable bottles for guests with a package. Confirm availability and conditions on MSC Musica for this sailing with MSC; don't count on an included bottle without that confirmation.

entries.title: How long can I stay in my cabin on Monday?
entries.text: The cabin must be vacated early so the next cruise can be prepared. Follow the time MSC announces on board; 10:00 AM is only a reference and doesn't guarantee you can use the cabin until then. Plan breakfast, luggage and documents for disembarkation.

entries.title: How do I organize my luggage for disembarkation?
entries.text: Follow the disembarkation instructions and tags provided by MSC, including the procedure for collecting your bags. Pack what you need for the last night and the following morning in your carry-on. Make sure you have all your bags at the terminal and review the meeting instructions for your transportation.

entries.title: Do all companions need to be in the group? Who should I contact?
entries.text: Add your cabin companions and family members to the official group so they receive the announcements. Ask the person in charge, through the channel already shared, to add them; the charter bus group is a separate channel for those who booked that transportation. For vouchers, cabin details and bookings, message Júnior/Royal Trip privately. For games, the event schedule and the kit, talk to our team and the game teachers.

entries.title: What are the boarding date and times?
entries.text: Boarding is on November 20 (Friday) at the Port of Santos, with a reference check-in window of 9 AM to 3 PM. Disembarkation is on November 23 (Monday), starting at 7 AM. These times are for reference: follow the arrival window and instructions on your booking voucher and MSC's announcements on board.

entries.title: What do I need to have with me at boarding?
entries.text: Bring your printed boarding voucher and your original ID in good condition, with a photo that allows identification. For Brazilian citizens on this domestic itinerary, MSC accepts the RG (Brazilian ID card), CNH (Brazilian driver's license), passport and other civil documents listed in its official rules, and does not require the RG to have been issued less than ten years ago. The digital CNH must be opened in the official app; photos, screenshots and copies, even certified ones, do not replace the document. We also recommend bringing the physical document. For minors, check with Royal Trip which documents and consent forms are required depending on who is traveling with them. Foreign guests must confirm with the agency the documents that apply to their nationality.

entries.title: When can I check in?
entries.text: Royal Trip handles the group's check-in. After the announcement in the WhatsApp group, the person responsible for each cabin should message Júnior/Royal Trip privately to request the official vouchers and luggage labels. Check the details of every passenger and print the documents before boarding.

entries.title: Do I need to be vaccinated to board?
entries.text: Check the current health requirements for your sailing with Royal Trip and MSC. Don't rely on old vaccination or antigen-test rules as current instructions: requirements may change depending on the health situation, the destination and the authorities. Follow the official guidance you receive for your boarding.

entries.title: How do I check my luggage, and when?
entries.text: Dropping off your luggage is the first thing to do when you arrive at the port. If you're driving, luggage drop-off is very close to the parking lot.

entries.title: Is there transportation to the port?
entries.text: Yes! We offer an official round-trip charter bus between Barra Funda (São Paulo), at Rua Tagipuru, near no. 552, and the Port of Santos. Bus 1: meet at 6:00 AM, departure at 6:30 AM (confirmed). Bus 2: meet at 6:40 AM, departure at 7:20 AM, subject to a minimum number of passengers; if the minimum isn't reached, a full refund will be issued via Pix (Brazil's instant payment system). The return from the port on Monday (Nov 23) is scheduled for 10:30 AM. See the charter bus and book your seat.

entries.title: How do I handle parking?
entries.text: You need to book a parking spot in advance to avoid it being full. Details on the Concais parking lot and hotel suggestions are here on the site, in the Transportation & Accommodation section.

entries.title: Who is Royal Trip?
entries.text: Royal Trip is the event's official partner travel agency, with more than 14 years in air and sea travel, plus themed cruises, corporate events and weddings on ships. CNPJ 16.957.402/0001-19.

entries.title: What is the MSC Musica's itinerary?
entries.text: Departure from Santos (SP) on Nov 20, bound for Búzios (RJ), returning to Santos on Nov 23.

entries.title: Can pregnant guests or babies sail on the cruise?
entries.text: MSC does not allow travel if a pregnancy reaches 24 weeks at any point during the cruise. Pregnant guests below that limit must present a medical certificate stating gestational age, expected due date, and confirmation of a low-risk pregnancy and fitness to travel, with the doctor's CRM (Brazilian medical license number), signature and stamp. Let Royal Trip know in advance so they can forward the documents and review your booking. Babies can join this mini-cruise, but they must be listed on the cabin booking; confirm fares and fees with the agency.

entries.title: Will there be a room for playing games?
entries.text: Yes! The Crystal Lounge is the planned venue for Kriativos On Board. We'll confirm the room and hours in the group and in the event schedule. Tables are open and shared on a rotating basis among participants.

entries.title: Which games will be available?
entries.text: The official game library is organized in the Board Game Guru app. You'll find hundreds of modern games from our partners, and Encounter's game teachers will be there to teach you the rules. You can also bring your own games!

entries.title: How does the games app work, and how do I enter the giveaways?
entries.text: We use the official Board Game Guru app (available for Android and iOS). In the app, open the Kriativos On Board page and confirm your early check-in by tapping "Eu vou" ("I'm going"). This step is essential to enter the giveaways of games and exclusive prizes on board! In the app you can also browse the game library, see which game teachers teach each title and register in advance the games you'll bring on board (with direct import from Ludopedia or BoardGameGeek).

entries.title: Can I bring my own games and prototypes?
entries.text: Yes! You can bring as many games as you like, plus prototypes and new releases to play with the community.

entries.title: Can I take games to other areas of the ship?
entries.text: Yes, to any area except the restaurants (the tables are for meals). The game is your responsibility: when you take it out of the room, leave your name and cabin number so it can be checked when you return it.

entries.title: Until what time is the game room open?
entries.text: The idea is to play a lot during the day and at night. The room's hours will be confirmed in the group and in the schedule. On Sunday night, we'll let you know the deadline for returning games and clearing the tables for the final inventory.

entries.title: How does Wi-Fi work, and how do we communicate on board?
entries.text: MSC's satellite internet package is purchased separately for browsing the external internet. When you connect to the ship's internal Wi-Fi network, you can use the MSC for Me app and its free chat. Add "Kriativo" to your profile name or nickname so your friends can find you! During the port call in Búzios, there may be 4G/5G signal from Brazilian carriers, depending on coverage and your location. Check the day of the port call in your booking's official itinerary.

entries.title: Is the safety drill mandatory?
entries.text: Yes. Complete the mandatory procedure MSC indicates for your boarding; the crew will tell you the place, time and steps, including instructions in the app. Watching a video or opening the app alone doesn't fulfill every requirement.

entries.title: How is a board game cruise different from other events?
entries.text: Kriativos On Board combines the love of games with a complete vacation at sea. You enjoy full board, cabin accommodation, the leisure of a luxury ocean liner and a space dedicated to games, according to the event schedule, to play and make lifelong friends.

entries.title: What's included in my booking?
entries.text: Accommodation in your chosen category and full board (breakfast, lunch and dinner), plus water, tea and coffee at the buffet restaurants, subject to availability.

entries.title: Is food unlimited on the ship?
entries.text: Yes. The main restaurants (buffet) serve daily meals: breakfast, lunch and dinner. If you can't make the served dinner time, you can eat at these buffets.

entries.title: How does dinner work on the ship?
entries.text: The main restaurant serves à la carte dinner in pre-assigned sittings, shown on your cruise card, with a starter, main course and dessert. Arrive on time: the 15-minute grace period refers to kitchen orders. If you miss your sitting, check the buffet and pizzeria options; the pizzeria usually runs almost 24 hours. Check the times in MSC's daily schedule.

entries.title: Can I sit at the same dinner table as friends from other cabins?
entries.text: You can ask. Tables for the à la carte dinner are assigned at check-in. To bring family and friends from other cabins to the same table for the cruise, go to the restaurant's maître d' right after boarding on the first day (Friday afternoon) with all the cabin numbers and ask to combine tables. The staff will confirm whether there's still room at dinner.

entries.title: Do I have to buy a drink package?
entries.text: No, it's optional. If someone in the cabin buys a package, the other guests must follow MSC's rules: adults with the same package and children/teens with the Non-Alcoholic package for kids, according to their age group. Babies don't need a package. Confirm with Royal Trip the conditions that apply to your cabin and the deadline to buy.

entries.title: What drink packages are available for adults?
entries.text: Non-Alcoholic, Easy and Premium Extra. Easy and Premium Extra include a maximum of 15 alcoholic drinks per person per day; MSC's daily period runs from 6 AM to 6 AM the next day. Confirm with Royal Trip the prices, discounts, installments and conditions available at the time of purchase.

entries.title: Do I get a minibar in the cabin with the Premium package?
entries.text: All MSC Musica cabins have a minibar, but minibar items are NOT included in any drink package (not even Premium Extra) and are charged separately to your cabin account. Tip: you can pick up canned or bottled drinks at the bars included in your package and keep them in your cabin's minibar to enjoy whenever you like.

entries.title: What does the cabin provide, and what should I pack?
entries.text: Cabins provide bed linen, towels, liquid soap, shampoo, a hair dryer, TV, air conditioning and a safe; check with the agency which amenities your booked category includes. What you MUST bring: toothbrush and toothpaste, hair conditioner, sunscreen and a compatible plug adapter, if needed. Also remember to pack comfortable clothes for game time, smart casual attire for the à la carte dinner (tank tops and flip-flops are not allowed), white clothes for the White Party and themed/neon pieces for the 80s Night!

entries.title: Do I need formal wear for dinner?
entries.text: No. For dinner, wear smart casual attire; the main restaurant doesn't allow tank tops or flip-flops. Check the ship's guidance for each venue and evening.

entries.title: How do I pay for onboard spending? Can I use US dollars?
entries.text: Onboard purchases are charged to the account linked to your cabin card (Cruise Card). Confirm with MSC or at reception which payment methods are accepted to link or settle this account, the currency and whether deposits are possible. If you'll use an international credit card, enable international use and bring the physical card.

entries.title: Is travel insurance mandatory?
entries.text: Insurance is optional and recommended for unexpected events and medical expenses. The approximate price is R$ 112 per person; confirm the policy and terms with Royal Trip before buying.

entries.title: Is there a kids' club or children's activities on the ship?
entries.text: Yes! MSC's Doremi Club offers supervised activities for children and teens by age group. Hours are usually long, around 9 AM to 11 PM, and should be checked in the daily schedule on board. Potty-trained children can stay with the youth staff; children who still wear diapers can use the spaces with their parents or guardians.

entries.title: I take medication that needs refrigeration. What should I do?
entries.text: Let Royal Trip know in advance, through a private channel, so they can forward your request to MSC and confirm the arrangements. Don't count on the cabin minibar keeping the temperature your medication requires, and carry your medication in your hand luggage.

entries.title: What can't I bring on board?
entries.text: MSC prohibits bringing on board any beverages, alcoholic or not (the exception is factory-sealed water for medical devices or infant formula), weapons, sharp objects such as blades and scissors, illegal drugs (including medical marijuana), flammable materials and explosives, and items that heat up or have an open flame, such as clothes irons, kettles, candles and incense. Hair dryers and hair straighteners are allowed. Drones may be carried if stored in the cabin, but using them on board is prohibited. Inflatables, such as air mattresses and rafts, can't be inflated on board. Alcohol bought in onboard shops or ashore is held by security until the end of the cruise. For food, MSC allows commercially packaged dry snacks as an exception. Prohibited items found at screening are confiscated and not returned; check the full official list and the conditions for special needs.

entries.title: What parties will there be on the ship?
entries.text: We'll have two unforgettable theme nights: the classic White Party (bring something white) and the 80s Night (retro style, accessories and neon colors to celebrate on Sunday night). Themed outfits aren't mandatory, but they make the experience on board even more fun! Check times and venues in the schedule.

entries.title: A 16-deck ocean liner for unforgettable days
entries.text: MSC Musica the world aboard a cruise ship Day and night, MSC Musica features live music, theater shows, bars and lounges, a casino, spa, and a dedicated kids' area. At the center of it all: an exclusive gaming lounge, available according to the event schedule, for the Kriativos.

entries.title: All-Inclusive Experience
entries.text: Cabin accommodation, full dining, and the entire MSC Musica amenities are all taken care of. Plus, enjoy the private game room according to the event schedule exclusively for KOB attendees.

entries.title: Documents and travel consent for minors
entries.text: What do you need to bring to board? What documents are required? Júnior: Since this is a domestic route (Santos to Búzios), you can use an RG (Brazilian ID card) or a CNH (Brazilian driver's license), digital or physical, as long as it's valid and has a recognizable photo. - Digital CNH: ATTENTION! A screenshot is NOT accepted! If you show the digital version, you must open the official CNH app on the spot, in front of the inspector. If the internet fails or the app goes down, you'll be stuck. So, preferably, bring the PHYSICAL DOCUMENT. - Photocopies: Neither certified copies nor plain photocopies are accepted. - Old RG: For domestic trips, MSC doesn't require the RG to be less than 10 years old, as long as it's in good condition and the photo clearly identifies the holder (it can't be a photo of you as a baby or a 3-year-old). - Minors not traveling with their parents: If you're bringing a nephew or niece, a grandchild or any minor traveling without one or both parents, a travel consent form is mandatory. Júnior provides the correct template to participants. Travel consent for minors depends on who accompanies them. Check your case with Royal Trip.

entries.title: Cruise Card, cards and onboard spending
entries.text: Spending and the cabin card (Cruise Card): On board, you don't use cash or bank cards for purchases at the bars, shops or casino. Everything is charged to your cabin card (your cabin key). - You can register an international credit card through the MSC for Me app, at the interactive kiosks or at the ship's reception. - Physical international cards are accepted: Visa, Mastercard and American Express, plus global accounts such as Wise and Nomad (it's best to bring the physical card with a chip, since contactless payment with your phone may fail if there's no signal). - MSC installments: MSC lets you pay onboard spending in installments (over $100 in up to 6 installments; over $300 in up to 10 installments on a credit card). - Free Shop / Duty Free: Open on board with good prices on perfume, drinks and electronics while the ship is sailing in international waters. entries.title: Dinner with friends in other cabins
entries.text: So, let's say I'm going with my wife, my sister and her husband, and my brother-in-law with my nephew. We're in several cabins. What's assigned here is per cabin. If you want to sit together at dinner, on the very first day, when you board, you need to stop by reception and ask where the maître d' is. They'll tell you where the maître d' will be and at what time. Then one person from each cabin goes to the maître d' and says: "We're a group and we want to sit together." Then he puts you together at the same dinner table. It has to be done on the first day. Once the first dinner has passed, forget it: you'll stay where you are. The à la carte restaurant is really nice for the experience Karen mentioned. The dishes are very refined and really tasty. You sit down, the waiter comes, hands you the menu, you choose a starter, main course and dessert, and you can order again. At first I didn't get it; I didn't like it, it took a while, the portion was small. We also affectionately call the self-service the cafeteria. The cafeteria upstairs will be open: go up and you can eat again. There'll be snacks going around too. The pizzeria will be open. So don't worry about food. That's it. And if you really liked a dish, no problem, they're serving you right there and you can order it again, but ideally you order everything up front, because they have everything scheduled in the kitchen. entries.text: remembering the schedule, there's the time you'll have dinner. It's either 7:15 PM or 9:30 PM. If you arrive more than 15 minutes late for the time on your card, you can't go in for dinner anymore. You'll have to eat at the cafeteria. At the cafeteria. Why? Because the waiter waits those 15 minutes, everyone sits down, he comes, takes everyone's order, and then the kitchen downstairs starts preparing and sending out the dishes. So if you arrive late, you delay the whole table, because when the waiter serves, he serves the starter to everyone. Until everyone finishes eating, he doesn't clear and serve the next course. entries.title: Travel insurance and medical expenses
entries.text: Health / travel insurance: - It isn't mandatory, but it's highly recommended. The onboard medical center charges in dollars at very high international rates (just the initial consultation is around USD 50, and simple procedures such as dressings or treatment can reach USD 800–USD 1,000 / R$ 5,000+). - Travel insurance with MSC's official insurer costs R$ 112 per person and provides medical coverage of US$ 40,000 (or R$ 40,000), plus coverage for luggage damage and cancellation. - Exclusive condition for Kriativos: the insurer kept the extended coverage for 29 cancellation reasons even if purchased later (up to 20 days before boarding). The spoken coverage amount and currency are ambiguous. Check the current policy and offer with Royal Trip.

entries.title: Children and the kids club
entries.text: MSC kids' facilities: - MSC's official kids club is called Doremi Club, divided by age group (Doremi Kids from 6 to 11, Teens from 11 to 17). - Long daily hours (usually 9 AM to 11 PM). - Diaper rule: To stay with the youth staff without a parent, the child must already be potty-trained. entries.title: Luggage
entries.text: Luggage rules: - MSC's formal limit: up to 3 suitcases per passenger (up to 90 kg in total). There are no weighing scales at the Port of Santos. MSC rule: per person, two suitcases of up to 23 kg and two carry-ons of up to 10 kg; per cabin, up to 100 kg and/or eight pieces. Beyond that, MSC says luggage isn't accepted at check-in. In Royal Trip's experience, there has never been a problem or a weigh-in at Santos; bringing more is at your own risk.
